thread.title: Apple's New iPhones Could Give Consumers 'Sticker Shock' | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple's New iPhones Could Give Consumers 'Sticker Shock' | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Apple 's ( AAPL ) new iPhones are priced higher than expected as the company pushes deeper into the premium segment of the smartphone market, analysts said Thursday.
X Apple introduced its 12th-generation smartphones at a media event Wednesday at its corporate headquarters in Cupertino, Calif. The new handsets include the iPhone XS, XS Max and XR, with the X standing for the Roman numeral 10. Apple watchers on Twitter joked that the names sound like the iPhone "Tennis," "Tennis Match" and "Tenor."
Hardware specifications for the new iPhones were as expected, thanks to media leaks, but the higher pricing surprised analysts.
Mizuho Securities analyst Vijay Rakesh said the starting prices for the iPhone XS and XS Max gave him "sticker stock."
Higher Prices Could Crimp Unit Sales "The iPhone specifications were mostly as expected though the price points were at the high end of most expectations, which while still early could crimp sell-through," he said in a report to clients.
The iPhone XS starts at $999 and the XS Max starts at $1,099. Both will be available for preorder starting Friday and will ship beginning on Sept. 21. The iPhone XS features a 5.8-inch OLED screen, while the XS Max has a 6.5-inch OLED screen. The new handsets boast improved cameras and speedier processors.
The iPhone XR starts at $749. It will be available for preorder on Oct. 19 and start shipping on Oct. 26. The XR has a 6.1-inch LCD screen and improved components.
"The big surprise was around pricing," RBC Capital Markets analyst Amit Daryanani said in his note to clients. "IPhone XS Max/XS/XR start at $1,099/$999/$749 respectively vs. last year's iPhone X/8+/8 lineup of $999/$799/$699."
IPhone Pricing Might Peak With New Handsets Apple is likely to see a boost in average selling prices with the new iPhone lineup, Macquarie Capital analyst Ben Schachter said in his note. He now expects average selling prices for the iPhone to rise 4% in 2019, up from his prior view of down 2%.
KeyBanc Capital Markets analyst Andy Hargreaves said iPhone pricing might peak with the current lineup. Consumers have shown a willingness to pay for larger screen sizes, but Apple is at the limit in reasonable display sizes with the new models, he said.
Apple dominates the premium smartphone segment, research firm IHS Markit said in a report Wednesday. It accounted for 86% of sales of smartphones priced above $751 in 2017. Samsung was second with 12% of the market.
At its fall product launch event, Apple also introduced its fourth-generation smartwatches. The Apple Watch Series 4 features larger display sizes and enhanced health and fitness applications. It is the first smartwatch capable of taking electrocardiograms. The watches start at $399 and will go on sale on Sept. 21.
Investors appeared unimpressed with Apple's latest product introductions, at least initially. Apple stock fell 1.2% to 221.07 on Wednesday. However, it jumped 2.4% to 226.41 on the stock market today .
Apple stock received at least six price-target hikes from Wall Street analysts following its product launch event.
